teaser.en: Its swept-back petals look like flickering flames, and every part of this beautiful lily is deadly poisonous.

summary.en: *Mpewa* is the flame lily, a climbing lily with wavy red-and-yellow flowers. It is one of the showiest wild flowers of the coast and also one of the most poisonous.

about.en:
*Mpewa* climbs by tendrils at the very tips of its leaves, which hook onto grass and twigs. The leaves are narrow and glossy.

The flowers are the star: six narrow, wavy-edged petals sweep backwards, yellow at the base and red towards the tips, with long stamens jutting out. As the flowers age they deepen towards crimson. The plant dies back to a fleshy underground tuber in the dry season and reappears with the rains.

All parts of *mpewa*, and especially the tuber, are very poisonous. The plant contains colchicine, and the tuber can be mistaken for an edible yam, so it is a plant worth knowing for safety.

where.en: Look for *mpewa* in bushland and along forest edges, scrambling through grass and low shrubs. It is easiest to see after the rains, when it is in flower.

uses.en: No specific Digo use has been recorded.

names.en: Digo: *mpewa*. English: flame lily or glory lily. No Swahili name has been recorded. Scientists call it *Gloriosa superba*.

reason.en: Another red-flowered climber of forest edges
A yam whose tuber could be confused with a poisonous one
